newsitem.title: GERMANY: German holiday market seen growing only 2pct in 97.
newsitem.headline: German holiday market seen growing only 2pct in 97.

text.p: The German package holiday market is likely to grow at only two percent in 1997, the country's second-largest tour operator, NUR Touristic, said.
NUR chairman Wolfgang Beeser said high unemployment and reserved consumer spending would hold down German holiday sales this year in contrast to previous years.
The German package holiday market is estimated by travel industry sources to be worth more than 21 billion marks ($13.1 billion) with more than 20 million holidays sold each year.
"We expect a small market growth of two percent. For ourselves, we expect seven percent growth," Beeser told a news conference.
NUR winter bookings were up 6.6 percent at present but summer bookings were not as strong as last year, Beeser noted.
The Karstadt AG subsidiary aimed to increase sales of its budget holiday brand to 150,000 passengers this year compared to 140,000 in 1995-96, he added.
NUR increased sales by 9.4 percent to 3.47 million holidays and improved turnover by seven percent to 3.6 billion marks in the November 1995-October 1996 fiscal year.
This meant it gained market share last year at the expense of Touristik Union International (TUI), the largest German tour operator, Beeser said.
Large tour operators were increasingly dominating the European travel market with TUI now market leader in the Netherlands and Airtours Plc dominating in Scandinavia, he added.
NUR Touristic had thus decided to merge its Belgian and Dutch subsidiaries into a single company, Neckermann Benelux, to strengthen its position.

Austria and Poland were other countries which would soon see competition between leading European tour operators, Beeser forecast. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017 ($ = 1.601 German Marks)
